page.description: EndeavourOS editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: An Arch Linux-based desktop with a graphical installer, a small set of preconfigured tools and the Arch repositories, so a rolling system can be installed in minutes.
pros: Arch Linux with a graphical installer and a working desktop after first boot.
Rolling release, with the Arch repositories unchanged.
Several desktop choices at install time, not one fixed ISO.
Small default package set: little to remove.
cons: Rolling updates need attention, as on any Arch system.
No LTS branch and no versioned support window.
x86_64 only for the main ISO.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for EndeavourOS; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the ISO to a USB stick, boot it and use the graphical installer. Writing erases the stick; the installer partitions or erases the target disk.
